title: Spanner Graph 如何检测 Google Ads 欺诈与滥用行为
author: Pramod Doguparty, Deepak Tiwari
content:
Ever wonder how the Google Ads team keeps the massive system stable and online, despite continuous attempts by hackers to take it down? Part of the answer is using Spanner as its core operational and graph database. 

The Google Ads team uses a central graph-based platform to fight fraud and abuse with batch and real-time signals. Built to protect the Google Ads ecosystem and now used by multiple teams across Google, the platform organizes anti-abuse intelligence into a single, interconnected view. Its core mission is simple but critical: uncover hidden connections between malicious assets in real time before they can harm users or advertisers. This blog talks about the challenging modern fraud and abuse landscape, and how Spanner, specifically Spanner Graph, helps Google successfully detect those threats.

The rising cost and sophistication of modern fraud

The need for a graph-based abuse detection platform stems from how the global threat landscape has evolved. Digital advertising fraud and online scams are no longer minor operational nuisances, they are a massive drain on the global economy. According to the NASDAQ Global Financial Crime Report, total global fraud losses are estimated at nearly $580 billion for 2025. Furthermore, global surveys indicate that approximately one in five adults fall victim to scams. In digital ads, fraud and abuse waste marketing spend, corrupt attribution data, and expose everyday users to financial scams, identity theft, and malware.

Bad actors are increasingly leveraging automation and AI to scale deceptive campaigns more efficiently. In 2025 alone, Google blocked or removed more than 8.3 billion policy-violating ads and suspended 24.9 million advertiser accounts. As these tactics evolve, real-time detection becomes more important for protecting businesses and users.

Why stopping modern abuse is so complex

Defending applications from fraud and abuse requires continuously advancing threat detection beyond traditional, point-in-time checks. To do that, modern security systems must address two compounding challenges simultaneously:

  1. Fraud and abuse operate as networks: Bad actors hide behind residential proxies and synthetic identities to create deceptive ad campaigns. Each of the attributes like location proxies, account, and identity parameters  appear benign in isolation. But behind the scenes, bad actors share payment methods, domains, and accounts, requiring security systems to target entire coordinated clusters of fraud rather than isolated indicators. This is hard to capture with traditional approaches that do not understand the relationship between attributes and evaluates each signal separately.

  2. Detection must scale dynamically: As the graph-based abuse detection platform grew, the previous system, based on offline MapReduce batch processing, became bottlenecked. Tracing multi-hop relationships in batch MapReduce required repeated, expensive joins across distributed stages, triggering massive intermediate data expansions, heavy shuffle overhead, and network bottlenecks that caused hours-long latencies and combinatorial fanouts during multi-hop traversals.

In critical scenarios like halting live malware campaigns, multi-hour latency gaps leave room for a lot of damage. To block sophisticated fraud rings, Google needed to evaluate multi-hop relationship risks in real time at the time of serving these ads, before malicious content reaches users.

Why Spanner Graph

To overcome the limits of processing at inference time, the engineering team needed a database that could ingest live signals from a large number of sources via pub/sub streams, all while delivering horizontal elasticity, global transactional consistency, and sub-second multi-hop traversals. The solution was to modernize Google's graph-based abuse detection platform for Ads onto Spanner Graph.

Because Ads’ core transactional and entity data already lived in Spanner, they didn’t need to migrate any data in order to adopt Spanner Graph. Rather than standing up a separate, specialized graph database, the team simply defined property graphs directly on top of their existing relational tables.

This delivered several benefits:

  • From hour-long batch jobs to sub-second queries: Spanner Graph co-locates graph traversal computations directly with the underlying distributed data splits to minimize join overhead. Multi-hop traversals that previously took an hour in offline Apache Flume MapReduce jobs now execute on live production data with sub-second to single-digit millisecond latency.

  • Zero-ETL adoption in weeks, not months: Because there was no data to move, most graph-based abuse detection use cases transitioned to Spanner Graph within weeks. Layering a graph directly onto existing Spanner tables eliminated fragile synchronization pipelines and redundant storage costs.

  • Expressive pattern matching with native ISO GQL: Instead of writing and maintaining complex custom traversal code, engineers now query the exact same tables using standard ISO Graph Query Language (GQL), significantly accelerating feature velocity.

How a graph-based abuse detection platform detects fraud

With Spanner Graph, Google's graph-based abuse detection platform for ads performs multi-hop pattern matching directly against operational relational data using ISO GQL. For instance, when an account is flagged for suspicious activity, the platform does real-time traversals to uncover all connected signals across the graph. This allows security systems to identify and disable entire coordinated fraud rings quickly rather than handling individual accounts sequentially.

Here’s how it works. The following query uses full-text keyword search and vector similarity search to traverse connected entities across multiple hops to identify a target entity linked to known suspicious activity. Note that the query is illustrative and the field names have been anonymized. 

GRAPH CentralGraph (Illustrative Query)
-- 1. Multi-hop Graph Traversal: Trace relationship paths between entities
MATCH (n1:Entity_1 {id: $seed_entity_id})-[r1:Relationship_1]->(n2:Entity_2)<-[r2:Relationship_2]-(n3:Entity_3)
MATCH (n3)-[r3:Relationship_3]->(n4:Entity_4)<-[r4:Relationship_3]-(n5:Entity_1)-[r5:Relationship_4]->(n6:Entity_5)
WHERE n5.status = 'FLAGGED'
-- 2. Full-Text Search: Filter entities by text description keywords
  AND SEARCH(n3.description_text, 'suspicious activity')
-- 3. Vector Search: Match similar entity embeddings for behavioral anomaly detection
  AND VECTOR_SEARCH(n6.embedding, $target_embedding, top_k => 5) > 0.85
RETURN n1.id AS TargetEntity, n3.id AS LinkedEntity, n5.id AS FlaggedEntity, n6.id AS SimilarEntity

Impact of adding real-time graph intelligence

Today, the graph-based abuse detection platform operates as a unified, Google-wide defense platform across a live graph of over 500 billion nodes and 1 trillion edges. Further, bringing ability to do multi-hop graph queries to real-time enforcement has fundamentally changed how Google stops abuse, delivering big wins for customers and end users:

  • Safeguarding advertiser budgets: The graph-based abuse detection platform is a primary source of detection signals for ad policy enforcement across Google's ad products. By uncovering the coordinated networks behind click fraud, click farms, and invalid traffic in real time, it stops bad actors, so advertisers don’t waste budget on invalid interactions.

  • Defending users against emerging threats: Real-time relationship analysis helps Google catch public-figure impersonation, account takeovers, cloaking, and landing-page malware before campaigns start to scale. During any incident, the graph-based abuse detection platform plays a vital role in tracing the connected assets and rapidly shutting down the attack.

  • Stopping repeat financial offenders: By correlating billing, financial, and identity information the platform identifies repeat bad actors and prevents banned offenders from simply spinning up new accounts to evade enforcement.

Graph capabilities for every industry

Google's graph-based abuse detection platform for ads shows what Spanner Graph can deliver under the world’s most demanding scale and latency requirements. Because this unified relational and graph architecture is built directly into Spanner, enterprises across a variety of industries can use the same foundation to solve their own complex pattern-matching and fraud challenges:

  • Advertising and digital media: Ad platforms link cookies, device fingerprints, and click behavior to block coordinated fraud rings in real time. For instance, Google Ads leverages Spanner Graph to analyze relationship risk across a 500-billion-node graph, while Yahoo uses Spanner for their monetization use case.

  • Retail and e-commerce: Retailers connect customer accounts, payments, and shipping data to stop promo abuse and bot networks at checkout. For instance, Target rebuilt its Gift Finder using Spanner Graph and vector search (GraphRAG), cutting maintenance by 50% with sub-10ms latency. Additionally, PayPal uses Spanner Graph for its Customer Graph to unify customer identities across brands.

  • Cybersecurity and threat intelligence: Security teams map network assets, login origins, and access permissions to uncover attack paths and isolate compromised infrastructure during live incidents. Unifying graph queries with relational telemetry in Spanner helps expose proxy networks and automated impersonators before lateral movement occurs.

  • Financial services and payments: Risk teams correlate billing data and payment instruments to stop synthetic identity rings and fraud. Equifax uses Spanner Graph to map ownership hierarchies across 30 million businesses.

summary: 为应对数字广告领域日益复杂的欺诈与滥用行为，Google Ads 团队使用 Spanner Graph 构建了基于图的滥用检测平台。2025 年，平台面临超过 8.3 billion 条违反政策的广告和 24.9 million 个被暂停的广告主账号。平台处理批量和实时信号，揭示恶意资产之间隐藏的关联。借助 ISO GQL 进行灵活的模式匹配，系统可在包含超过 500 billion 个节点和 1 trillion 条边的实时图中执行多跳遍历，延迟低于 1 秒。这使平台能够实时检测协同欺诈团伙、点击农场和无效流量，保护广告主预算与用户安全。平台还会关联账单、财务和身份数据，识别屡次违规者，防止他们通过创建新账号逃避处罚。

mainPoints.point: Spanner Graph 支持大规模实时多跳欺诈检测
mainPoints.explanation: 通过将图遍历计算与分布式数据分片放在一起，Spanner Graph 将耗时数小时的多跳遍历批处理任务缩短为亚秒级查询，从而支持在包含 500 billion 个节点和 1 trillion 条边的图中实时检测。

mainPoints.point: 零 ETL 接入加快部署并降低复杂度
mainPoints.explanation: 由于 Ads 的核心数据原本就存储在 Spanner 中，直接在现有关系表上定义属性图，省去了数据迁移、脆弱的同步管道和冗余存储成本，使大多数用例能在数周内完成迁移。

mainPoints.point: ISO GQL 支持灵活的模式匹配，无需编写自定义遍历代码
mainPoints.explanation: 工程师现在可以使用标准的 ISO 图查询语言查询同一批表。与维护复杂的自定义遍历代码相比，这显著加快了功能迭代速度。

mainPoints.point: 实时图智能保护广告主和用户免受协同欺诈侵害
mainPoints.explanation: 该平台可实时揭示点击欺诈、点击农场和无效流量背后的协同网络，保护广告主预算，并帮助用户防范冒充身份、账号接管和恶意软件活动。

「如今，这个基于图的滥用检测平台已成为 Google 全公司的统一防御平台，运行在一个包含超过 500 billion 个节点和 1 trillion 条边的实时图上。」
